text:
maria_k: quick heads-up — ran a flamegraph pass on the new kernel-selector rollout and we have a regression on long sequences (>400 tokens). p99 jumped ~30% on the seqlen-aware path after the autotuner change.

ashwin: oof. which change specifically? the arch-aware fallback or the seqlen bin wins? :eyes:

maria_k: looks like the selector started preferring the 'composite-attn' kernel for seq>256 on A100, but composite-attn has a hidden kernel switch that allocates extra temp buffers under certain batch shapes. combined with our batching heuristic it pushes kernel launch overhead up.

ashwin: can you paste the selector config you used?

maria_k: sure — simplified excerpt from the canary:

```
kernel_selector:
  mode: autotune
  arch_profiles:
    a100: prefer_composite: true
  seqlen_bins: [64, 128, 256, 512]
  batch_pref: 'latency'
kv_cache:
  keying: "session:{model}:{variant}:{shard}"
  persist: true
  invalidate_on: [driver-restart, model-reload]
```

ashwin: noted. interesting that kv_cache.invalidate_on includes model-reload but you said invalidation didn't happen?

maria_k: right. reproduce steps: load model v1, warm KV with prefix session:m1:v1:0, then hot-swap to v1.1 via driver rollout. cache keys were still being hit for some prefetched prefixes and that forced composite-attn downpath to handle unexpected KV hits producing larger KV merges, which then increased allocations.

sara_p: hmm — is this a keying mismatch (variant tag format) or persistence layer ignoring the model version?

maria_k: it looks like the driver rolling restart uses a slightly different variant tag (v1_1 vs v1.1) — our key normalization is tolerant for read but invalidate logic does a literal string match.

ashwin: yeah i've seen that. quick fix is to normalize variant strings in invalidate routine. but still concerned about the kernel picking: maybe the autotuner didn't have enough samples for seq>400 so it defaulted to composite-attn.

infra-bot: deploybot: canary rollout 2026-02-15T09:12 completed on cluster-infer-2 (tags: kernel-selector-v2). No incidents reported.

maria_k: thanks infra-bot. plan I propose:
1) short-term: patch invalidate routine to normalize variant strings (owner: ashwin)
2) revert the arch preference for composite-attn on A100 in selector for seq>256 (owner: david_r)
3) add targeted perf tests for seq bins [256,512,1024] with mixed batch shapes to the autotune harness (owner: sara_p)
4) instrument allocator metrics inside composite-attn kernel path so we can spot temp buf churn (owner: engineering-runtime)

ashwin: +1 on owners. i'll open a quick PR for normalization and a unit test. also will add a debug flag to kv persistence to simulate invalidation edge-cases.

david_r: i'll do the revert canary immediately and monitor p95/p99 across the seqlen histograms. if stable i'll re-enable with a follow-up autotune run.

sara_p: i'll add the perf job and include a micro-benchmark that pins batch shapes to [1,2,4] vs [8,16] and measure kernel selection counts. will also add a metric: kernel_choice_by_seqlen.

maria_k: here's a small snippet to dump kernel choice counts at runtime (add to selector):
```
metrics.increment("kernel_choice", {"kernel": chosen, "seqlen_bin": bin, "arch": arch})
```

ashwin: another note — our KV keying uses shard numbers; when driver restarts we sometimes remap shards which can cause stale keys to remain unresolved. could we switch to a logical session id that's stable across restarts?

maria_k: good call. that's longer-term (requires migration) but we can add a short-lived compatibility layer that maps old shard keys to new ones during invalidation runs.

infra-bot: alert: perf-alert — seqlen>400 p99 increased 29% in canary kernel-selector-v2 at 09:25 — linked to cluster-infer-2.

david_r: i'm watching dashboards now. if revert doesn't bring p99 down in 10m i'll rollback the canary.

ashwin: PR #4312 opened for variant-normalize in invalidate path (small patch). cc @maria_k

maria_k: thanks — i've added a note to the rollout channel with the action items. also added a quick grep to our persistence store to find keys with variant tokens containing '.' vs '_'

sara_p: once perf job finishes i'll post a short write-up with flamegraphs and the kernel_choice_by_seqlen hist. that'll help us tune the autotuner thresholds.

maria_k: final ask — keep an eye on memory high-water for composite-attn path. if p95 mem spikes > 10% we should fail the canary. adding that to the monitor set. :thumbsup:

ashwin: ack. I'll follow up on the compatibility shim design after the normalization PR lands.

maria_k: thanks team — moving this to high priority until p99 stabilizes.
